lines.trans: Seeing that she even blew off an event, people are asking whether Cindy went into hiding.
If she went into hiding, could there be a man?
Bingo, it is a man! She got a boyfriend, stopped listening to her CEO, and disappeared!
Then could the guy be a celebrity—an idol?
I know who is dating whom among almost every idol, and Cindy is not one of them.
A second-generation conglomerate heir, then?
That has to be it! Because she is dating a tycoon, she is unafraid of penalty fees and blew off the event!
Then could she be off at some luxury hotel in Paris right now with that conglomerate heir?
What conglomerate heir… talking when they do not even know.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.
Then let's meet tomorrow.
Then we're at the same company!

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

맞다.gloss: to be right, to be correct

meanings.note: Used to confirm facts or answers.

meanings.en: to fit, to suit, to match

examples.trans: Yes, that's my phone number.
These shoes fit my feet perfectly.

meanings.en: to be unable to, cannot do
meanings.note: Expresses inability; follows a noun in 말 못하다 (cannot say).

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.
Did you hear about this idol?
I was busy today because of idol.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

examples.trans: Still, you have to go to the corporate event the day after tomorrow—the penalty fee is steep.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay
